note: The lint-pool check, scripts/check-lint-pool.py, run after M1-88 was committed: its pass was owed, since every task since M1-08 has one, and was run with M1-89's. Each mutant switches off one fault the check exists for, or bends the depth rule; the judges are its self-test and the real check against this tree. A Python script needs no build, but the harness always builds, so every mutant names orbsim_shaders, the cheapest target that always builds, as a no-op. The pool itself -- the CMake that declares it -- is judged by lint_pool too: removing JOB_POOL from a lint step is its first mutant. **Run twice on 2026-09-27.** First: 6 caught and 1 survived -- 'no lint steps at all is accepted', because the self-test's case for that fault also declared no pool and was reported for that instead, so it tested nothing of its own. The case was given a correct pool (its own commit). Second run: 7 of 7 caught, none invalid, none hung; the CMake mutant is caught by lint_pool against the real tree. **Renamed by M1-96, 2026-09-28**: the pool is orbsim_memory, the script check-memory-pool.py and its tests memory_pool and memory_pool_self_test; the mutants are the same.

mutants.name: a lint step leaves the pool
one job per 2 GiB instead of 3
the floor of one job is lost
a missing pool is not reported
a step outside the pool is accepted
no lint steps at all is accepted
mutants.find: found.append("no lint steps found -- the check would be checking nothing")
